section_content: All full-time employees who have completed a minimum of six months of continuous service with the organization are eligible for annual leave. Part-time employees working at least 20 hours per week become eligible after completing 12 months of continuous service. Contract employees and interns are not eligible for annual leave under this policy. Eligibility is determined based on the employee's hire date as recorded in the HR management system. Employees on a Performance Improvement Plan may have their annual leave requests reviewed by their department head before approval.

Eligible full-time employees are entitled to 18 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year. Part-time employees receive a prorated entitlement based on their contracted hours relative to a standard 40-hour work week. Unused annual leave up to a maximum of 5 days may be carried forward to the following calendar year, but carried-forward days must be used before March 31. Any unused carried-forward leave that is not used by this deadline will lapse automatically. Employees who join mid-year receive a prorated entitlement based on the number of remaining complete months in the calendar year.

Annual leave requests must be submitted through the internal Employee Self-Service portal at least 10 working days before the intended start date. Requests for leave exceeding 5 consecutive working days require a minimum of 20 working days advance notice. All leave requests must include the start date, end date, total number of days requested, and a brief reason for leave. The direct supervisor will receive an automatic notification and must respond to the request within 3 working days. If the supervisor does not respond within the stipulated timeframe, the request will be escalated to the department head for action.

Annual leave may not be taken during designated organizational blackout periods, which include the final two weeks of each financial quarter and the first week of January. The HR department will publish the annual blackout period calendar by December 1 of the preceding year. No more than 30 percent of a team's members may be on annual leave simultaneously. If multiple employees request the same dates, priority is given based on the date the request was submitted, followed by the employee's length of service. Exceptions to blackout period restrictions require written approval from the division director.

Approved annual leave may be cancelled or modified by submitting a revised request through the Employee Self-Service portal at least 5 working days before the original start date. Cancellations made less than 5 working days before the leave start date require direct approval from the supervisor and must include a written justification. Cancelled leave days are returned to the employee's available balance immediately upon cancellation approval. If the organization requires an employee to cancel approved leave due to critical business needs, the employee will receive priority consideration for future leave requests covering the same period. Repeated cancellation of approved leave by the employee may be flagged for review by the HR department.

All employees, including full-time, part-time, and contract staff, are eligible for sick leave from their first day of employment. Full-time employees are entitled to 12 days of paid sick leave per calendar year. Part-time employees receive a prorated entitlement based on their contracted working hours. Contract employees receive 6 days of paid sick leave per calendar year. Unused sick leave days do not carry forward to the next calendar year and will lapse on December 31 of each year. Sick leave is intended solely for genuine illness or medical appointments and must not be used as a substitute for annual leave or personal leave.

Employees must notify their direct supervisor of any sick leave absence before the start of the scheduled work shift or as soon as reasonably possible thereafter. Notification must be provided by phone call, email, or through the Employee Self-Service portal. Text messages are accepted only if the supervisor has explicitly agreed to receive notifications by this method. If the employee is unable to make the notification personally due to the severity of their condition, a family member or designated emergency contact may provide the notification on their behalf. Employees must provide a daily update if the absence extends beyond the initially reported period.

A medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner is required for any sick leave absence exceeding 2 consecutive working days. The medical certificate must include the date of consultation, the recommended period of absence, and confirmation that the employee is unfit for work. Medical certificates must be submitted to the HR department within 3 working days of the employee's return to work. Failure to submit the required medical documentation may result in the absence being recorded as unauthorized leave without pay. The organization reserves the right to request a medical certificate for absences of 2 days or fewer if a pattern of frequent short absences is identified.

section_heading: Extended Illness and Return to Work
section_content: Employees who are absent due to illness for more than 10 consecutive working days must provide a fitness-to-return certificate from their treating physician before resuming duties. The HR department may arrange a return-to-work meeting to discuss any adjustments or accommodations needed for the employee's safe return. If an employee exhausts their paid sick leave entitlement and requires additional time off due to continuing illness, they may apply for unpaid medical leave with approval from the HR director. Employees on extended sick leave will continue to receive their standard benefits for a period of up to 90 calendar days from the first day of absence. Beyond 90 days, benefits continuation will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

section_heading: Sick Leave Abuse and Disciplinary Action
section_content: The organization takes sick leave abuse seriously and monitors absence patterns to identify potential misuse. Indicators of potential abuse include frequent absences on Mondays or Fridays, absences immediately before or after public holidays, and patterns of absence that coincide with denied annual leave requests. Employees identified as potentially abusing sick leave will be invited to an informal discussion with their supervisor and an HR representative. If abuse is confirmed following the discussion, the employee will receive a formal written warning. Repeated confirmed abuse of sick leave may result in further disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment, in accordance with the organization's disciplinary procedures.

All leave requests must be approved by the employee's direct supervisor before the leave can be taken. If the direct supervisor is unavailable, the approval authority is delegated to the next-level manager within the same department. Leave requests exceeding 10 consecutive working days require additional approval from the department head. Leave requests that fall within designated blackout periods require approval from the division director, regardless of the number of days requested. The HR department retains override authority to approve or deny any leave request where organizational policy compliance is in question.

Supervisors must respond to all leave requests within 3 working days of receipt. If the supervisor does not respond within 3 working days, the request is automatically escalated to the department head, who must respond within an additional 2 working days. If neither the supervisor nor the department head responds within the combined 5-working-day window, the leave request is automatically approved. Emergency leave requests, such as those related to bereavement or sudden illness, must be reviewed and responded to within 1 working day. The HR department will generate weekly reports of pending unanswered leave requests and distribute them to the relevant managers.

Leave requests must be evaluated based on the following criteria in order of priority: the employee's remaining leave balance, operational requirements and staffing levels for the requested period, the number of team members already approved for leave during the same period, and the advance notice provided by the employee. Supervisors must not deny leave requests based on personal preference or as a form of informal disciplinary action. All leave denials must include a written explanation specifying which of the above criteria was not met. Employees have the right to appeal a denied leave request by submitting a written appeal to the HR department within 5 working days of receiving the denial.

All leave requests, approvals, denials, and cancellations must be recorded in the centralized HR management system. Supervisors are responsible for ensuring that their team's leave records are accurate and up to date. The HR department will conduct quarterly audits of leave records to ensure compliance with organizational policies. Any discrepancies identified during the audit will be reported to the relevant department head for resolution. Leave records must be retained for a minimum of 7 years in accordance with the organization's data retention policy. Employees may request a summary of their leave history by submitting a request through the Employee Self-Service portal.

In exceptional circumstances, such as natural disasters, public health emergencies, or government-mandated lockdowns, the organization may temporarily modify leave approval procedures. Temporary modifications to this policy must be approved by the Chief Human Resources Officer and communicated to all employees within 2 working days of the decision. Employees who are unable to submit leave requests through the standard electronic system due to system outages or technical failures may submit requests by email to their supervisor and the HR department simultaneously. Retroactive leave requests are permitted only in cases of documented emergencies and must be submitted within 5 working days of the employee's return to work. All retroactive requests must be accompanied by supporting documentation.
